extracted.intended_audience: F99/K00 applicants, mentors, and NIH grant reviewers in aging/ADRD research
extracted.subtask_description: A training plan and sponsor/co‑sponsor statements for an NIH F99/K00 career development application describing mentor qualifications, responsible conduct training, specific training goals, institutional resources, mentorship structure, coursework, internships, and dissemination expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor/mentor qualifications and mentoring record
rubrics_metrics.description: Mentors' prior mentoring history and expertise (e.g., Dr. Dodge: mentored 17 PhD/postdocs and four career development awardees; Dr. Kaye: 25 years mentoring, 27 previous PhD/postdocs; Dr. Palinkas: extensive publication record in mixed-methods; Dr. Silbert: neuroimaging expertise; Dr. Wu: 15 mentees).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use mentors with documented history of mentoring trainees and complementary, relevant expertise across disciplines (Neurology, Biostatistics, Engineering, Anthropology, Social Work). Provide counts of previous mentees and career development award mentorships as evidence of mentoring success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary mentor role & specific training content
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary mentor (Dr. Dodge) will be the primary mentor in the postdoctoral stage, providing training in developing clinical trial designs, recruiting underserved populations, selecting clinical trial outcomes, clinical trial enrichment, and analyses of high-frequency digital biomarker longitudinal data; assist in familiarizing the trainee with dementia research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly specify primary mentor responsibilities by stage (F99 vs K00) and list concrete methodological and substantive skills the primary mentor will provide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor-provided research support and access to data/resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors have active grants and initiatives (e.g., I-CONECT, CART, ORCATECH, OADC cores, pilot funding opportunities) available to the trainee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document specific projects, cores, datasets, and funding (grant numbers/names) that the trainee can access for hands-on research and pilot studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR) instruction venues
rubrics_metrics.description: USC SSW provides RCR instruction via (a) research methods courses; (b) professoriate workshops and scholarly lectures; (c) Hamovitch Center; and (d) IRB research training courses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List multiple institutional venues for RCR training and how they complement each other.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCR course subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Courses cover ethical research conduct, conflict of interest, protecting human subjects, community-based/collaborative research practices, peer review, publication ethics and authorship, responsibilities to humanity, avoiding and handling misconduct, and ethical/unethical study designs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure RCR curriculum explicitly covers this broad set of topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCR course format, faculty participation, duration and frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: Format: small in-person group discussions (7–8 students). Faculty participation: Tenure-track faculty instruct all courses. Duration: meet weekly for 3–4 hours for the semester. Frequency: PI completed three courses in specified terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide details on class size, instructor type, weekly hours, and historical trainee participation to demonstrate depth of instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional development workshops and scholarly lectures
rubrics_metrics.description: Format: face-to-face discussion among doctoral students. Subject matter: publishing ethics, authorship, peer reviews, data collection/analysis, study design, grant proposals, financial award use, and managing collaborative teams. Duration: 1–2 hour workshops scheduled monthly; attendance mandatory for doctoral students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include frequency, duration, topics, and mandatory attendance when describing PD offerings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hamovitch Center consultation and offerings
rubrics_metrics.description: Hamovitch Center provides scholarly workshops, lectures, and individual consultation from full-time professionals covering all aspects of conducting research; workshops/lectures scheduled semiquarterly and consultations available as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe center services, staff expertise, scheduling cadence, and trainee engagement examples (data analysis consultation, manuscript writing, study design, grant proposals).

rubrics_metrics.name: IRB and compliance online trainings and refreshers
rubrics_metrics.description: IRB online courses completed include Human Subjects, Good Clinical Practice, Conflicts of Interest, and HIPAA Privacy Education. These are required for proposed studies with periodic refresher training (examples: refresher in December 2019; planned refresher December 2022).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify required online modules, completion dates, and schedule for refresher training to demonstrate compliance preparedness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital scholar/digital research training
rubrics_metrics.description: CTSI Digital Scholar Training Program: online webinars monthly about digital research practices (selecting journals, industry collaboration, participant recruitment using non-traditional approaches); webinars ~1 hour with Q&A; PI has attended ~9 webinars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document trainee engagement with digital research training opportunities and frequency of offerings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentoring structure, frequency, and coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: Mentoring plan includes biweekly meetings with Dr. Dodge in F99, weekly meetings in K00; quarterly meetings with all sponsors; in-person annual meetings at major scientific meetings; mentors coordinate communication between USC and OHSU sponsors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a timeline of mentoring frequency by training stage and explicit plans for team coordination (quarterly/all-sponsor meetings, annual in-person convenings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentored clinical internship experiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Two mentored internship experiences at USC and OHSU; named supervisors (e.g., Dr. John Ringman as F99 internship supervisor; Dr. Kaye for K00 clinical internship at a memory clinic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include internship sites, supervisors, and which training stage each internship occurs to show clinical immersion opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailored coursework to meet training needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Selected courses include a cognitive decline and ADRD special topics course at USC Leonard Davis School of Gerontology, and a course on systematic review and meta-analysis; also planned R programming course.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List specific coursework, rationale for selection relative to trainee's gaps, and timing within training stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hands-on methodological training and lab participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Attend OADC imaging core weekly lab meetings; collaborate with mentors (Drs. Dodge and Silbert) to gain hands-on experience analyzing biomarker outcomes and digital biomarkers using I-CONECT and CART data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe concrete lab attendance, data analysis projects, and mentor-supervised hands-on activities to develop methodological competence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical and programming skill development
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop efficiency in statistical analysis by taking R programming course; build on strengths in SEM and MLM modeling to conduct longitudinal analyses with NHATS data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify target statistical methods, programming languages/courses, and how these will be applied to dissertation and pilot projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mixed-methods and implementation science mentoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Dr. Palinkas will assist with purposeful sampling for mixed-methods research, data collection and analysis plans, and provide consultation on implementation/dissemination science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail mentorship in mixed-methods design and implementation considerations, including frequency of consultations (biweekly) and expected deliverables (manuscripts, intervention proposals).

rubrics_metrics.name: Development and pilot-testing of community-based interventions
rubrics_metrics.description: K00 stage proposes developing and pilot testing a community-based intervention to provide sustainable solutions for social connectedness and dementia prevention; training includes co-design, recruitment, and pilot grant preparation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outline steps for intervention development (mixed-methods formative work, focus groups, pilot funding application) and mentor support for design/implementation/evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exposure to technology-enabled interventions and devices
rubrics_metrics.description: Training to explore mobile apps, ambient technology, wearable devices, virtual reality, and ambient sensors; collaborations to observe VR intervention sessions and to use digital biomarker data from CART and I-CONECT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe planned technology exposures, observation/participation in sessions, and integration of digital biomarker data into intervention design and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication, presentation, and dissemination expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Trainee will apply skills to write dissertation, seek to publish in high-impact journals (The Gerontologist, Journal of Gerontology, Journal of Alzheimer’s Disease), submit abstracts, and present at conferences (AAIC, GSA, CTAD).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State concrete dissemination targets (journals, conferences) and mentor support for manuscript drafting and presentation preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunities for specialized coursework in clinical trial methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Plans to take an online UCSF course on study design for intervention research and to apply for NINDS clinical trial methodology course (R25NS088248) for two years of continuous training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include enrollment plans for specialized trial-methodology courses and how they fit into the trainee's K00 preparation and funding application strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to institutional cores and investigator meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: Access to OADC cores (neuroimaging, outreach/recruitment/education, data management) and attendance at monthly OADC investigator meetings (via Zoom in F99 and in-person in K00) to observe grant presentations and network.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document core-access procedures, meeting attendance plans, and networking opportunities to integrate trainee into intellectual community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentorship contributions to manuscript and grant development
rubrics_metrics.description: Mentors will collaborate on drafting and publishing manuscripts using I-CONECT data, prepare pilot grant applications at OHSU, and provide constructive feedback on theoretical reasoning and intervention design in weekly mentoring meetings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify mentor roles in writing and grant preparation, expected frequency of feedback, and planned co-authorship or supervisory arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence of trainee fit with sponsor environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Description of how the trainee's research interests match USC and OHSU emphases (e.g., USC SSW resources, membership in Edward R. Roybal Institute on Aging and USC ADRC; OHSU Layton Aging and ADRC alignment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain alignment between trainee goals and institutional strengths, including membership/access to institutes and how they will support training aims.
